title: Characterizing Privacy Risks of Quantum Machine Learning with Emergent Quantum-Native Access
abstract: arXiv:2609.05702v2 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) has shown rapid advances by utilizing quantum computing for machine learning tasks. Meanwhile, the privacy risks accompanying QML is also starting to be studied, which inherit privacy leakage channels from "classical" ML and also quantum-unique risks. Existing work on privacy-preserving QML largely focuses on a QML-as-a-service scenario, which generally assumes that the QML model owner provides only classical bit outputs to queries, while users (and adversaries) have only classical computing abilities. translated_title: 新兴量子原生访问下量子机器学习隐私风险的刻画
translated_abstract: 量子机器学习（QML）通过利用量子计算执行机器学习任务而取得了快速进展。与此同时，伴随QML产生的隐私风险也开始受到研究关注，这些风险既继承了“经典”机器学习的隐私泄露渠道，也包含量子独有的风险。现有的隐私保护QML研究主要聚焦于QML即服务（QML-as-a-service）场景，该场景通常假设QML模型所有者仅向查询提供经典比特输出，而用户（及攻击者）仅具备经典计算能力。然而，在一个量子原生世界中，具备量子能力的用户/攻击者可能同时拥有量子计算能力并能访问服务提供商量子信息输出，这使得上述假设日益受到挑战。本文旨在通过研究针对QML模型的成员推断攻击来弥合这一差距，证明随着量子访问权限和量子计算能力的提升……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 本文突破了以往假设攻击者仅有经典计算能力的局限，首次系统刻画了在用户/攻击者具备量子计算能力和量子信息访问权限的量子原生场景下，量子机器学习模型（如成员推断攻击）所面临的隐私风险。
en_tdlr: This paper characterizes the privacy risks of Quantum Machine Learning models, such as membership inference attacks, in a quantum-native setting where users/adversaries possess quantum computing capabilities and access to quantum information outputs, moving beyond prior work that assumed attackers have only classical abilities.
